articles.title: NCRTC opens Sahibabad-Modipuram stretch for pier and portal advertising
articles.description: New Delhi: The National Capital Region Transport Corporation (NCRTC) has invited bids for advertising rights on piers and portal structures along the Sahibabad-Modipuram section of the Delhi-Meerut Namo Bharat corridor. NCRTC is a joint venture of the Government of India and the governments of Delhi, Haryana, Rajasthan and Uttar Pradesh. The advertising inventory covered by the tender extends across more than 50 km and passes through residential areas, commercial centres and markets in Ghaziabad and Meerut. According to NCRTC, the corridor currently handles around 1.1 lakh commuters a day and has recorded more than 4.5 crore passenger journeys. The selected licensee will be responsible for the design, fabrication, installation, operation and maintenance of the advertising infrastructure under the terms of the tender. The Delhi-Ghaziabad-Meerut Namo Bharat corridor spans about 82 km between Sarai Kale Khan in Delhi and Modipuram in Meerut. Meerut Metro services also operate on the Namo Bharat infrastructure between Meerut South and Modipuram. Bidders can participate through the e-tendering process. NCRTC said tender details, eligibility requirements and timelines are available on its website and the Central Public Procurement Portal.

articles.title: Modi's governance model: Scaling trust, efficiency and growth
articles.description: Governance transformation relies on technology and citizen engagement for efficient delivery. Digital identity and direct transfers have improved welfare program efficiency significantly. Decriminalizing regulations and reducing compliance burdens foster ease of living for entrepreneurs. Government e-marketplace enhances transparency and access to public demand for businesses. This governance model is becoming an economic asset for India's growth.

articles.title: Leh Workshop Helps MSMEs Explore Public Procurement, Finance And Export Opportunities
articles.description: Leh Workshop Helps MSMEs Explore Public Procurement, Finance And Export Opportunities Leh, Sep 16 (KNN) A national-level workshop in Leh on Tuesday familiarised local entrepreneurs and artisans with public procurement, Government e-Marketplace (GeM) onboarding, quality certification, financing and export promotion opportunities available to micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs). The one-day workshop was aimed at helping businesses access government procurement opportunities, improve product quality and packaging, secure institutional finance and explore national and international markets. Focus On Government Procurement And Quality The technical sessions covered MSME Ministry schemes, vendor registration and public procurement procedures, including presentations by officials from GeM, NSIC and POWERGRID. Representatives from the Bureau of Indian Standards (BIS) and Quality Council of India (QCI) briefed participants on BIS certification, Zero Defect, Zero Effect (ZED), Quality Control Orders and quality requirements for public procurement. The Indian Institute of Packaging (IIP) also conducted a session on packaging, highlighting its relevance to market access and exports. Entrepreneurs Briefed On Finance, Exports The workshop also covered export promotion, with officials from the Directorate General of Foreign Trade (DGFT) outlining opportunities and procedures for exporters. SIDBI officials briefed participants on financing schemes, while the Khadi and Village Industries Commission (KVIC) highlighted credit-linked financing through the Prime Minister’s Employment Generation Programme (PMEGP) portal. The session also covered value addition and infrastructure upgradation for key Ladakh products, including pashmina, apricot and seabuckthorn. Push For Local Products To Reach Wider Markets Administrative Secretary, Industries and Commerce Department, UT Ladakh, Himanshu Gupta, highlighted MSME schemes including the Credit Linked Capital Subsidy Scheme and PMEGP. He also said the UT Administration was exploring a credit scheme to support aspiring entrepreneurs. Director, Planning, Tsewang Gyalson, urged local entrepreneurs to leverage Ladakh’s resources and explore national and international markets for locally produced goods. The workshop also stressed the importance of Udyam Registration for accessing MSME schemes and encouraged entrepreneurs to regularly use official online portals to stay updated on government programmes. The workshop was organised by the MSME Development and Facilitation Office (MSME-DFO), Jammu, under the Ministry of MSME. (KNN Bureau)
